records.literal_gloss: They called there: Pharaoh king of Egypt [is] a noise; he has let pass the appointed time.

en.L: They called out there, \q "Pharaoh king of Egypt [is but] a noise; \q he has let the appointed time pass by."
en.B: There they cried out, \q "Pharaoh king of Egypt is only a loud noise; \q he has let his moment pass."
en.R: There they say, \q "Pharaoh king of Egypt is just a lot of noise. \q He missed his chance."

es.L: Allí gritaron: \q «El faraón, rey de Egipto, [no es más que] ruido; \q dejó pasar el tiempo señalado».
es.B: Allí gritaban: \q «El faraón, rey de Egipto, no es más que mucho ruido; \q dejó pasar su oportunidad».
es.R: Allí dicen: \q «El faraón, rey de Egipto, no es más que puro ruido. \q Perdió su oportunidad».

fr.L: Ils ont crié là : \q « Le pharaon, roi d’Égypte, [n’est qu’]un bruit ; \q il a laissé passer le moment fixé. »
fr.B: Là, ils ont crié : \q « Le pharaon, roi d’Égypte, n’est qu’un grand bruit ; \q il a laissé passer son heure. »
fr.R: Là-bas, ils disent : \q « Le pharaon, roi d’Égypte, ne fait que du bruit. \q Il a laissé passer sa chance. »

sw.L: Walipiga kelele huko, \q "Farao mfalme wa Misri [ni] kelele tu; \q ameuacha wakati ulioamriwa upite."
sw.B: Huko walilia, \q "Farao mfalme wa Misri ni kelele kubwa tu; \q ameiacha nafasi yake ipite."
sw.R: Huko wanasema, \q "Farao mfalme wa Misri ni kelele nyingi tu. \q Ameikosa nafasi yake."

vi.L: Ở đó chúng kêu lên: \q "Pha-ra-ôn vua Ai Cập [chỉ là] một tiếng ồn ào; \q hắn đã để lỡ thời điểm đã định."
vi.B: Ở đó chúng kêu lên: \q "Pha-ra-ôn vua Ai Cập chỉ là tiếng ồn ào; \q hắn đã để lỡ thời cơ."
vi.R: Ở đó chúng nói: \q "Pha-ra-ôn vua Ai Cập chỉ to tiếng mà thôi. \q Hắn đã bỏ lỡ cơ hội."

ko.L: 그들이 거기서 외쳤다. \q "이집트 왕 바로는 [한낱] 소음일 뿐, \q 정해진 때를 그냥 지나가게 했다."
ko.B: 그들이 거기서 외쳤다. \q "이집트 왕 바로는 시끄러운 소리일 뿐이다. \q 그는 자기 때를 놓쳐 버렸다."
ko.R: 그들은 거기서 이렇게 말한다. \q "이집트 왕 바로는 그저 큰소리만 친다. \q 그는 기회를 놓쳐 버렸다."

decisions.choice: a noise who let the appointed time pass: a mocking nickname for Pharaoh
alternatives: They called Pharaoh king of Egypt 'Noise, who let the appointed time pass'
decisions.reason: "Called" can mean "gave a name", as in 20:3, and the words that follow sound like a nickname: "Loud Noise, who let the appointed time go by". Pharaoh made a great din of threats and promises but missed his moment to act, as Isaiah called Egypt "Rahab who sits still" (Isaiah 30:7). The Greek translation reads "call the name of Pharaoh Neco", treating the words as a name; this is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: noise: the roar of a crowd or an army, a loud din
decisions.reason: The word is used of the roar of armies and of rushing waters (25:31; 48:45; Isaiah 17:12-13). Egypt, which rose roaring like the Nile (verses 7-8), turns out to be only sound.

decisions.choice: they called there: the soldiers who flee
decisions.reason: "They" are most likely the soldiers of verse 16, who shout this as they leave; "there" is the place of the defeat.

decisions.choice: [is but] a noise (Literal); only a loud noise (Balanced); just a lot of noise (Readable); let his moment pass / missed his chance
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the words as a saying about Pharaoh and gives "let the appointed time pass" in plain English at Balanced and Readable. The footnote gives the reading as a nickname (m1).

source.text: חַי־אָ֨נִי֙ נְאֻם־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ כִּ֚י כְּתָב֣וֹר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּכְכַרְמֶ֖ל בַּיָּ֥ם יָבֽוֹא׃

records.literal_gloss: [As] I live, declares the King, Yahweh of hosts [is] his name, surely like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea, he will come.

en.L: As I live, declares the King, \q whose name [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, \q surely like Tabor among the mountains \q and like Carmel by the sea, he will come.
en.B: As I live, declares the King, \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, \q one is coming who is like Tabor among the mountains, \q like Carmel by the sea.
en.R: As surely as I live, says the King, \q whose name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, \q someone is coming who towers like Mount Tabor over the mountains \q and like Mount Carmel over the sea.

es.L: Vivo yo, declara el Rey, \q cuyo nombre [es] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, \q que como el Tabor entre los montes \q y como el Carmelo junto al mar, vendrá.
es.B: Vivo yo, afirma el Rey, \q {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre, \q que vendrá uno que es como el Tabor entre los montes, \q como el Carmelo junto al mar.
es.R: Tan cierto como que yo vivo, dice el Rey, \q cuyo nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, \q viene alguien que se eleva como el monte Tabor sobre los montes \q y como el monte Carmelo sobre el mar.

fr.L: Je suis vivant, déclare le Roi, \q dont le nom [est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : \q oui, comme le Thabor parmi les montagnes \q et comme le Carmel près de la mer, il viendra.
fr.B: Aussi vrai que je suis vivant, déclare le Roi, \q dont le nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q quelqu’un vient, semblable au Thabor parmi les montagnes, \q semblable au Carmel près de la mer.
fr.R: Aussi vrai que je suis vivant, dit le Roi, \q dont le nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, \q quelqu’un vient qui domine tout, comme le mont Thabor domine les montagnes \q et comme le mont Carmel domine la mer.

sw.L: Kama niishivyo, asema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q hakika kama Tabori katikati ya milima, \q na kama Karmeli kando ya bahari, atakuja.
sw.B: Kama niishivyo, asema Mfalme, \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi ndilo jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, \q anakuja mmoja aliye kama Tabori katikati ya milima, \q kama Karmeli kando ya bahari.
sw.R: Kama niishivyo hakika, anasema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, \q anakuja mtu aliye juu kama mlima Tabori juu ya milima mingine, \q na kama mlima Karmeli juu ya bahari.

vi.L: Ta hằng sống, Vua phán vậy, \q danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, \q chắc chắn như núi Tha-bô giữa các núi \q và như Cạt-mên bên biển, nó sẽ đến.
vi.B: Ta hằng sống, Vua phán vậy, \q danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân: \q có một kẻ sẽ đến, như núi Tha-bô giữa các núi, \q như Cạt-mên bên biển.
vi.R: Thật như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hằng sống, Vua phán, \q là Đấng có danh là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, \q có một kẻ sẽ đến, sừng sững như núi Tha-bô vượt trên các núi \q và như núi Cạt-mên nhô cao trên biển.

ko.L: 내가 살아 있음을 두고 [맹세한다]. 왕의 선언이다. \q 그의 이름은 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다. \q 산들 가운데 다볼 같고, \q 바닷가의 갈멜 같은 자가 반드시 올 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 살아 있음을 두고 맹세한다. 왕이 말한다. \q 그의 이름은 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다. \q 산들 가운데 우뚝 솟은 다볼 산 같고, \q 바닷가의 갈멜 산 같은 자가 오고 있다.
ko.R: 내가 살아 있음을 두고 맹세한다. 왕이 말한다. \q 그 왕의 이름은 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다. \q 다볼 산이 산들 위로 우뚝 솟은 것처럼, \q 갈멜 산이 바다 위로 솟은 것처럼 높은 자가 오고 있다.

decisions.choice: as I live: an oath
decisions.reason: God swears by his own life, the most solemn oath there is (22:24; Numbers 14:21; Isaiah 49:18). What follows is certain.

decisions.choice: Tabor and Carmel: mountains that stand out above everything around them
decisions.reason: Mount Tabor rises alone out of the plain of Jezreel, and the ridge of Carmel stands high above the Mediterranean coast. The one who is coming stands out above every power in the same way.

decisions.choice: he will come: the conqueror, unnamed here
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject. The heading (verse 13) shows that it is Nebuchadrezzar, the one "coming" against Egypt; verses 20 and 24 speak of him as coming from the north.

decisions.choice: the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts
decisions.reason: Pharaoh is "king of Egypt" (verse 17), but the true King is the LORD (10:7, 10). The same title returns in 48:15 and 51:57.

decisions.choice: one is coming (Balanced); someone is coming who towers ... Mount (Readable); As surely as I live (Readable); the LORD of Armies is his name (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable words the oath "As surely as I live", the usual English form of this oath, and Balanced keeps the Hebrew order of the title, "the LORD of Armies is his name". Both also supply a subject for "he will come" (m3), and Readable adds "Mount" and "towers" to show what the comparison means (m2).

decisions.choice: Vivo yo (L, B); Tan cierto como que yo vivo (R)
decisions.reason: God's own oath, in the wording set in the Samuel note.

decisions.choice: danh Ngài (the King's name)
decisions.reason: The King speaks of his own name in the third person; Vietnamese keeps that, with the span on "Ngài". Tha-bô and Cạt-mên are the published forms.

decisions.choice: "왕의 선언이다" (L), "왕이 말한다" (B, R), and "그의 이름은 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다", without "-시-"
decisions.reason: The King here is God naming himself inside his own oath, so he takes no honorific (terms note); in God's mouth Readable says "거느린".

source.text: כְּלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת־מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־נֹף֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְנִצְּתָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Baggage of exile make for yourself, dweller daughter of Egypt; for Noph will become a waste and be laid in ruins, without inhabitant.

en.L: Make yourself baggage for exile, \q you who dwell [there], daughter of Egypt! \q For Memphis will become a waste, \q and it will be laid in ruins, without inhabitant.
en.B: Pack your bags for exile, \q you people of Daughter Egypt! \q For Memphis will become a wasteland, \q a ruin where no one lives.
en.R: People of Egypt, \q pack your bags to be taken away as prisoners! \q The city of Memphis will become an empty ruin. \q No one will live there.

es.L: Hazte equipaje para el destierro, \q tú que habitas [allí], hija de Egipto; \q porque Menfis será una desolación, \q y quedará en ruinas, sin habitante.
es.B: Prepara tu equipaje para el destierro, \q pueblo de la hija de Egipto; \q porque Menfis quedará desolada, \q en ruinas, sin que nadie viva en ella.
es.R: Pueblo de Egipto, \q prepara tus cosas, porque te llevarán prisionero. \q La ciudad de Menfis quedará en ruinas y vacía. \q Nadie vivirá allí.

fr.L: Fais-toi un bagage d’exil, \q habitante, fille de l’Égypte ! \q Car Memphis deviendra une désolation, \q et elle sera détruite, sans habitant.
fr.B: Prépare tes bagages pour l’exil, \q peuple de la fille d’Égypte ! \q Car Memphis deviendra un désert, \q une ruine où personne n’habite.
fr.R: Peuple d’Égypte, \q prépare tes bagages, car tu vas être emmené prisonnier ! \q La ville de Memphis deviendra une ruine vide. \q Personne n’y habitera plus.

sw.L: Jifanyie mizigo ya uhamisho, \q wewe ukaaye [huko], binti Misri! \q Kwa maana Memfisi itakuwa ukiwa, \q nao utaharibiwa kabisa, bila mkaaji.
sw.B: Fungeni mizigo yenu kwa ajili ya uhamisho, \q enyi watu wa Binti Misri! \q Kwa maana Memfisi itakuwa nyika, \q magofu yasiyo na mtu anayeishi ndani yake.
sw.R: Enyi watu wa Misri, \q fungeni mizigo yenu kwa sababu mtachukuliwa mateka! \q Mji wa Memfisi utakuwa magofu matupu. \q Hakuna mtu atakayeishi huko.

vi.L: Hãy sắm cho mình hành trang đi lưu đày, \q hỡi kẻ cư ngụ, con gái Ai Cập! \q Vì Mem-phít sẽ thành hoang phế, \q bị đổ nát, không còn dân cư.
vi.B: Hãy gói ghém hành trang đi lưu đày, \q hỡi dân cư của con gái Ai Cập! \q Vì Mem-phít sẽ thành chốn hoang tàn, \q một nơi đổ nát không người ở.
vi.R: Hỡi dân Ai Cập, \q hãy gói ghém hành trang để bị bắt đi làm tù binh! \q Thành Mem-phít sẽ thành đống đổ nát vắng tanh. \q Không ai sống ở đó nữa.

ko.L: 딸 이집트에 사는 자야, \q 포로로 끌려갈 짐을 꾸려라! \q 멤피스가 황무지가 되고, \q 불타 폐허가 되어 사는 사람이 없을 것이다.
ko.B: 딸 이집트의 백성아, \q 포로로 끌려갈 짐을 꾸려라! \q 멤피스가 황무지가 되고, \q 아무도 살지 않는 폐허가 될 것이다.
ko.R: 이집트 백성아, \q 포로로 끌려갈 짐을 꾸려라! \q 멤피스 성은 텅 빈 폐허가 될 것이다. \q 거기에 아무도 살지 않을 것이다.

decisions.choice: baggage of exile: the few things a captive could carry
decisions.reason: People taken into exile walked with a small bundle on their shoulders (Ezekiel 12:3-7). Egypt, which hoped to cover the earth, is told to get ready to be led away.

decisions.choice: dweller daughter of Egypt: the people of Egypt, pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: The two words are joined: the one who lives as Daughter Egypt, that is, the people of the land pictured as a woman (verses 11, 24; compare 48:18, "dweller daughter of Dibon").

decisions.choice: be laid in ruins: be destroyed so that nothing stands
decisions.reason: The verb is used of cities laid waste (2:15; 4:7). Memphis, the old royal city (verse 14), will be left without people.

decisions.choice: you people of Daughter Egypt (Balanced); People of Egypt ... to be taken away as prisoners (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom the words address (m2); Readable explains exile and adds "the city of".

source.text: עֶגְלָ֥ה יְפֵֽה־פִיָּ֖ה מִצְרָ֑יִם קֶ֥רֶץ מִצָּפ֖וֹן בָּ֥א בָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: A heifer very beautiful [is] Egypt; a gadfly from [the] north has come, has come.

en.L: A very beautiful heifer [is] Egypt; \q a gadfly from the north has come, has come!
en.B: Egypt is a lovely young heifer, \q but a gadfly from the north is coming, coming on!
en.R: Egypt is like a beautiful young cow. \q But a stinging fly from the north is coming to attack her!

es.L: Novilla hermosísima [es] Egipto; \q un tábano del norte viene, ¡viene!
es.B: Egipto es una hermosa novilla, \q pero un tábano del norte se acerca, ¡se acerca!
es.R: Egipto es como una vaca joven y hermosa. \q Pero un insecto que pica viene del norte a atacarla.

fr.L: Une génisse très belle, [c’est] l’Égypte ; \q un taon du nord est venu, il est venu !
fr.B: L’Égypte est une belle jeune génisse, \q mais un taon arrive du nord, il arrive !
fr.R: L’Égypte est comme une belle jeune vache. \q Mais une mouche qui pique arrive du nord pour l’attaquer !

sw.L: Misri [ni] mtamba mzuri sana; \q inzi wa kuuma kutoka kaskazini amekuja, amekuja!
sw.B: Misri ni mtamba mzuri mchanga, \q lakini inzi wa kuuma kutoka kaskazini anakuja, anakuja!
sw.R: Misri ni kama ng'ombe mchanga mzuri. \q Lakini inzi anayeuma kutoka kaskazini anakuja kumshambulia!

vi.L: Ai Cập [là] một con bò cái tơ rất đẹp; \q một con mòng từ phương bắc đã đến, đã đến!
vi.B: Ai Cập là một con bò cái tơ xinh đẹp, \q nhưng một con mòng từ phương bắc đang đến, đang lao tới!
vi.R: Ai Cập giống như một con bò cái tơ xinh đẹp. \q Nhưng một con ruồi trâu từ phương bắc đang đến đốt nó!

ko.L: 이집트는 아주 아름다운 암송아지다. \q 북쪽에서 쇠파리가 왔다, 왔다!
ko.B: 이집트는 아름다운 어린 암소다. \q 그러나 북쪽에서 쇠파리가 몰려온다, 몰려온다!
ko.R: 이집트는 아름다운 어린 암소와 같다. \q 그러나 북쪽에서 쏘는 파리가 그를 공격하러 오고 있다!

decisions.choice: gadfly: a biting fly that torments cattle
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It comes from a root meaning "to nip" or "pinch", and in a herd picture it most likely means a biting fly such as a gadfly or horsefly, which drives cattle wild. Others understand it as "destruction" or "one who cuts off". Either way, the enemy from the north attacks the sleek heifer.

decisions.choice: a very beautiful heifer: Egypt, sleek and well fed
decisions.reason: The rare doubled word means "very pretty". A young cow fattened in good pasture pictures a rich, untroubled land (compare Hosea 10:11; Amos 4:1). It may also glance at Egypt's honor for sacred cattle (verse 15).

decisions.choice: has come, has come: the Hebrew repeats the verb
decisions.reason: The doubled verb gives urgency: it is coming, it is here. Many Hebrew manuscripts and some ancient translations read the second word with one more letter, "has come against her". The meaning is close. This is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: lovely young heifer; coming, coming on (Balanced); like a beautiful young cow; stinging fly ... to attack her (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the doubled verb as "coming, coming on". Readable makes the picture a comparison, says "stinging fly" for gadfly (m1), and says what the fly will do.

decisions.choice: con mòng (L, B); con ruồi trâu (R)
decisions.reason: The gadfly is a biting fly that torments cattle; "mòng" names it, and Readable uses the more familiar "ruồi trâu".

source.text: גַּם־שְׂכִרֶ֤יהָ בְקִרְבָּהּ֙ כְּעֶגְלֵ֣י מַרְבֵּ֔ק כִּֽי־גַם־הֵ֧מָּה הִפְנ֛וּ נָ֥סוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו לֹ֣א עָמָ֑דוּ כִּ֣י י֥וֹם אֵידָ֛ם בָּ֥א עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Also her hired [soldiers] in her midst [are] like calves of [the] stall; for also they have turned, they have fled together, not they stood; for [the] day of their calamity has come upon them, [the] time of their punishment.

en.L: Even her hired soldiers in her midst [are] like calves of the stall; \q for they too have turned, they have fled together, they did not stand; \q for the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
en.B: Even the hired soldiers in her ranks are like fattened calves; \q they too have turned and fled together, they did not stand their ground; \q for the day of their disaster has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
en.R: Even the soldiers Egypt hired are like fat calves ready to be killed. \q They too turn and run away together. They do not stand and fight. \q The day of their disaster has come. It is time for them to be punished.

es.L: También sus mercenarios en medio de ella [son] como becerros de engorde; \q porque también ellos se volvieron, huyeron juntos, no se mantuvieron en pie; \q porque vino sobre ellos el día de su calamidad, el tiempo de su castigo.
es.B: Hasta los soldados que contrató son como becerros cebados; \q también ellos dieron la vuelta y huyeron juntos, no resistieron; \q porque les llegó el día de su desgracia, el tiempo de su castigo.
es.R: Hasta los soldados que Egipto contrató son como becerros gordos listos para el matadero. \q También ellos dan la vuelta y huyen juntos. No se quedan a pelear. \q Les ha llegado el día de la desgracia. Es hora de que sean castigados.

fr.L: Même ses mercenaires au milieu d’elle [sont] comme des veaux d’étable ; \q car eux aussi ont tourné le dos, ils se sont enfuis ensemble, ils n’ont pas tenu bon ; \q car le jour de leur désastre est venu sur eux, le temps de leur châtiment.
fr.B: Même les mercenaires qui sont dans ses rangs sont comme des veaux engraissés ; \q eux aussi ont tourné le dos et se sont enfuis ensemble, ils n’ont pas tenu bon ; \q car le jour de leur désastre est venu sur eux, le temps de leur châtiment.
fr.R: Même les soldats que l’Égypte a payés sont comme des veaux gras prêts à être abattus. \q Eux aussi font demi-tour et s’enfuient tous ensemble. Ils ne restent pas pour se battre. \q Le jour de leur désastre est arrivé. Le moment est venu de les punir.

sw.L: Hata askari wake wa kukodiwa walio katikati yake [ni] kama ndama wa zizini; \q kwa maana wao nao wamegeuka, wamekimbia pamoja, hawakusimama; \q kwa maana siku ya msiba wao imewajia, wakati wa kuadhibiwa kwao.
sw.B: Hata askari wa kukodiwa walio katika jeshi lake ni kama ndama walionenepeshwa; \q wao nao wamegeuka na kukimbia pamoja, hawakusimama imara; \q kwa maana siku ya maafa yao imewajia, wakati wa kuadhibiwa kwao.
sw.R: Hata askari ambao Misri iliwakodi ni kama ndama wanono walio tayari kuchinjwa. \q Wao nao wanageuka na kukimbia pamoja. Hawasimami kupigana. \q Siku ya maafa yao imefika. Ni wakati wa wao kuadhibiwa.

vi.L: Ngay cả lính đánh thuê giữa nó [cũng] như bò con trong chuồng; \q vì chúng cũng quay lưng, cùng nhau chạy trốn, chúng không đứng vững; \q vì ngày tai họa của chúng đã đến trên chúng, thời kỳ chúng bị phạt.
vi.B: Ngay cả lính đánh thuê trong hàng ngũ nó cũng như bò con được vỗ béo; \q chúng cũng quay lưng chạy trốn cả loạt, không đứng vững được; \q vì ngày tai họa của chúng đã đến, thời kỳ chúng bị trừng phạt.
vi.R: Ngay cả quân lính Ai Cập thuê mướn cũng như bò con mập béo sắp bị làm thịt. \q Chúng cũng quay lưng cùng nhau bỏ chạy. Chúng không đứng lại chiến đấu. \q Ngày tai họa của chúng đã đến. Đã đến lúc chúng bị trừng phạt.

ko.L: 그 가운데 있는 그의 품꾼들도 외양간의 송아지들 같다. \q 그들도 돌아서서 함께 도망하고 서지 못했다. \q 그들의 재앙의 날, 그들이 벌받을 때가 그들에게 닥쳤기 때문이다.
ko.B: 이집트 군대 안에 있는 용병들도 살진 송아지들 같다. \q 그들도 돌아서서 함께 달아나고, 버티지 못했다. \q 그들이 재앙을 당할 날, 벌받을 때가 닥쳤기 때문이다.
ko.R: 이집트가 돈을 주고 데려온 군인들도 잡아먹으려고 살찌운 송아지들 같다. \q 그들도 돌아서서 함께 달아난다. 그들은 버티고 싸우지 않는다. \q 그들이 재앙을 당할 날이 왔다. 그들이 벌을 받을 때가 되었다.

decisions.choice: hired soldiers: the foreign mercenaries in Egypt's army
decisions.reason: Egypt's army in this period relied heavily on hired troops from other lands, such as those named in verse 9. They are the ones who say "let us go back to our own people" in verse 16.

decisions.choice: calves of the stall: animals fattened for slaughter
decisions.reason: Calves kept in the stall were fed up to be killed for a feast (Amos 6:4; 1 Samuel 28:24). The well-paid soldiers are ready for the LORD's "sacrifice" (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the time of their punishment: the time when God calls them to account
decisions.reason: The noun is from the verb "to visit", used of God coming to deal with someone, here in judgment (8:12; 10:15; 11:23).

decisions.choice: fat calves ready to be killed
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the fattened calves picture (m2).

decisions.choice: "품꾼들" (L); "용병들" (B); "돈을 주고 데려온 군인들" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "hired men"; Balanced uses the modern word for mercenaries, and Readable explains it.

source.text: קוֹלָ֖הּ כַּנָּחָ֣שׁ יֵלֵ֑ךְ כִּֽי־בְחַ֣יִל יֵלֵ֔כוּ וּבְקַרְדֻּמּוֹת֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔הּ כְּחֹטְבֵ֖י עֵצִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Her sound like a snake [that] goes, for in strength they go, and with axes they come to her, like cutters of trees.

en.L: Her sound is like a snake that goes away, \q for they march in force \q and come against her with axes, \q like those who cut down trees.
en.B: She makes a sound like a snake slithering away, \q as her enemies march in force \q and come at her with axes, \q like woodcutters felling trees.
en.R: Egypt hisses like a snake as it slides away, \q because her enemies are coming with a strong army. \q They come at her with axes, \q like woodcutters cutting down trees.

es.L: Su sonido es como el de una serpiente que se va, \q porque marchan con fuerza \q y vienen contra ella con hachas, \q como los que cortan árboles.
es.B: Hace un ruido como de serpiente que se escabulle, \q mientras sus enemigos avanzan con fuerza \q y vienen contra ella con hachas, \q como leñadores que talan árboles.
es.R: Egipto silba como una serpiente que se escapa arrastrándose, \q porque sus enemigos vienen con un ejército poderoso. \q Vienen contra ella con hachas, \q como leñadores que cortan árboles.

fr.L: Sa voix est comme [celle d’]un serpent qui s’en va, \q car ils marchent en force \q et viennent contre elle avec des haches, \q comme ceux qui abattent les arbres.
fr.B: Elle fait entendre un bruit comme un serpent qui s’enfuit, \q car ses ennemis avancent en force \q et viennent contre elle avec des haches, \q comme des bûcherons qui abattent des arbres.
fr.R: L’Égypte siffle comme un serpent qui s’enfuit en glissant, \q parce que ses ennemis arrivent avec une armée puissante. \q Ils viennent contre elle avec des haches, \q comme des bûcherons qui coupent des arbres.

sw.L: Sauti yake ni kama ya nyoka aendaye zake, \q kwa maana wanakuja kwa nguvu, \q nao wanamjia na mashoka, \q kama wakataji wa miti.
sw.B: Anatoa sauti kama nyoka anayeteleza akikimbia, \q adui zake wanapokuja kwa nguvu \q na kumjia na mashoka, \q kama wakata miti wanaoangusha miti.
sw.R: Misri inazomea kama nyoka anayeteleza akikimbia, \q kwa sababu adui zake wanakuja na jeshi lenye nguvu. \q Wanamjia na mashoka, \q kama wakata miti wanaokata miti.

vi.L: Tiếng nó như tiếng con rắn bò đi, \q vì chúng kéo đến với lực lượng hùng mạnh, \q và mang rìu đến đánh nó \q như những kẻ đốn cây.
vi.B: Nó phát ra tiếng như con rắn trườn đi, \q khi quân thù kéo đến đông đảo \q và mang rìu đến đánh nó \q như tiều phu đốn cây.
vi.R: Ai Cập rít lên như con rắn đang trườn đi, \q vì quân thù kéo đến với một đạo quân hùng mạnh. \q Chúng mang rìu đến đánh nó \q như tiều phu chặt cây.

ko.L: 그의 소리가 기어가는 뱀 같다. \q 그들이 대군을 이끌고 진군하며, \q 도끼를 들고 그에게 온다. \q 나무를 찍는 자들처럼.
ko.B: 이집트는 기어서 달아나는 뱀처럼 쉿쉿 소리를 낸다. \q 원수들이 대군을 이끌고 진군하여 \q 도끼를 들고 그에게 쳐들어온다. \q 나무를 베는 나무꾼들처럼.
ko.R: 이집트는 미끄러져 달아나는 뱀처럼 쉿쉿 소리를 낸다. \q 원수들이 강한 군대를 이끌고 오고 있기 때문이다. \q 그들은 도끼를 들고 이집트에 쳐들어온다. \q 나무를 베어 넘기는 나무꾼들처럼.

decisions.choice: her sound like a snake that goes: the faint hiss of a snake escaping
decisions.reason: Egypt rose roaring like the Nile (verses 7-8) and Pharaoh was a "noise" (verse 17). Now all that is heard is the rustle and hiss of a snake slipping away through the undergrowth as the woodcutters come.

decisions.choice: they: the invaders from the north
decisions.reason: "They" are not named; they are the enemy of verses 20 and 24, the people of the north.

decisions.choice: with axes, like woodcutters: the army pictured as felling a forest
decisions.reason: The picture continues into verse 23: the invaders cut down Egypt like trees (compare 22:7; Isaiah 10:33-34, of Assyria).

decisions.choice: slithering away (Balanced); hisses ... slides away (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of sound and movement the picture means (m1); Readable supplies "hisses" and names Egypt.

source.text: כָּרְת֤וּ יַעְרָהּ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֖י לֹ֣א יֵֽחָקֵ֑ר כִּ֤י רַבּוּ֙ מֵֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין לָהֶ֖ם מִסְפָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: They have cut down her forest, declares Yahweh, though not it can be searched; for they are more numerous than locusts, and there is not to them number.

en.L: They have cut down her forest, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q though it cannot be searched out; \q for they are more numerous than locusts, \q and there is no number to them.
en.B: They will cut down her forest, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q dense as it is, \q for they are more than locusts; \q they cannot be counted.
en.R: They will cut down her forest, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q even though it is too thick to walk through. \q The enemy soldiers are more than a swarm of locusts. \q No one can count them.

es.L: Cortaron su bosque, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q aunque no se puede recorrer; \q porque son más numerosos que las langostas, \q y no tienen número.
es.B: Cortarán su bosque, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q por espeso que sea, \q porque son más que las langostas; \q no se pueden contar.
es.R: Cortarán su bosque, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q aunque es tan espeso que no se puede atravesar. \q Los soldados enemigos son más que una plaga de langostas. \q Nadie los puede contar.

fr.L: Ils ont abattu sa forêt, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q bien qu’elle soit impénétrable ; \q car ils sont plus nombreux que les sauterelles, \q et il n’y a pas de nombre pour eux.
fr.B: Ils abattront sa forêt, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q si épaisse soit-elle, \q car ils sont plus nombreux que les sauterelles ; \q on ne peut pas les compter.
fr.R: Ils abattront sa forêt, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q même si elle est trop épaisse pour qu’on puisse y passer. \q Les soldats ennemis sont plus nombreux qu’un nuage de sauterelles. \q Personne ne peut les compter.

sw.L: Wameukata msitu wake, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q ingawa hauwezi kupenyeka; \q kwa maana wao ni wengi kuliko nzige, \q wala hawana hesabu.
sw.B: Watakata msitu wake, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q ingawa ni mnene, \q kwa maana wao ni wengi kuliko nzige; \q hawawezi kuhesabika.
sw.R: Watakata msitu wake, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q ingawa ni mnene mno kupitika. \q Askari wa adui ni wengi kuliko kundi la nzige. \q Hakuna mtu awezaye kuwahesabu.

vi.L: Chúng đã đốn rừng của nó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q dù rừng ấy không thể dò thấu; \q vì chúng đông hơn cào cào, \q không thể đếm được.
vi.B: Chúng sẽ đốn rừng của nó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q dù rừng ấy rậm rạp đến đâu, \q vì chúng đông hơn cào cào, \q không thể đếm xuể.
vi.R: Chúng sẽ đốn rừng của nó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán, \q dù rừng ấy rậm rạp đến mức không ai đi qua được. \q Quân thù đông hơn cả một bầy cào cào. \q Không ai đếm được.

ko.L: 그들이 그의 숲을 베었다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. \q 그것을 헤아려 찾을 수 없지만, \q 그들이 메뚜기보다 많아서 \q 셀 수가 없기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그들이 그의 숲을 베어 버릴 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 그 숲이 아무리 빽빽해도 그럴 것이다. \q 그들은 메뚜기 떼보다 많아서 \q 셀 수가 없다.
ko.R: 그들이 이집트의 숲을 베어 버릴 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 그 숲이 너무 빽빽하여 지나갈 수 없어도 그럴 것이다. \q 적군은 메뚜기 떼보다 많다. \q 아무도 그들을 셀 수 없다.

decisions.choice: though it cannot be searched out: a forest too dense to go through
alternatives: for they cannot be searched out (counted)
decisions.reason: The verb means to search or explore (Job 5:9, of things beyond searching). The forest is so thick that no one can make their way into it, yet the invaders cut it down. The clause could instead be read with what follows, "for they cannot be counted", but that is said in the last line.

decisions.choice: her forest: Egypt's people and strength pictured as trees
decisions.reason: A forest stands for a nation's multitude and pride (21:14; Isaiah 10:18-19).

decisions.choice: more than locusts: a vast army
decisions.reason: Locust swarms were the picture of numbers beyond counting (Judges 6:5; 7:12; Nahum 3:15).

decisions.choice: will cut down
decisions.reason: The verb is past in form, describing the coming judgment as if done. Balanced and Readable put it in the future, which is what it means here; Readable adds "the enemy soldiers" for "they".

source.text: הֹבִ֖ישָׁה בַּת־מִצְרָ֑יִם נִתְּנָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד עַם־צָפֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Is put to shame [the] daughter of Egypt; she has been given into [the] hand of [the] people of [the] north.

en.L: The daughter of Egypt has been put to shame; \q she has been given into the hand of the people of the north.
en.B: Daughter Egypt is put to shame, \q handed over to the people of the north.
en.R: The people of Egypt will be disgraced. \q They will be handed over to the people from the north.

es.L: Avergonzada está la hija de Egipto; \q entregada en mano del pueblo del norte.
es.B: La hija de Egipto queda avergonzada, \q entregada al pueblo del norte.
es.R: El pueblo de Egipto quedará humillado. \q Será entregado a la gente del norte.

fr.L: La fille de l’Égypte a été couverte de honte ; \q elle a été livrée dans la main du peuple du nord.
fr.B: La fille d’Égypte est couverte de honte, \q livrée au peuple du nord.
fr.R: Le peuple d’Égypte sera couvert de honte. \q Il sera livré au peuple venu du nord.

sw.L: Binti Misri ametiwa aibu; \q ametiwa mkononi mwa watu wa kaskazini.
sw.B: Binti Misri ameaibishwa, \q amekabidhiwa kwa watu wa kaskazini.
sw.R: Watu wa Misri wataaibishwa. \q Watakabidhiwa kwa watu kutoka kaskazini.

vi.L: Con gái Ai Cập bị hổ thẹn; \q nó bị nộp vào tay dân phương bắc.
vi.B: Con gái Ai Cập bị sỉ nhục, \q bị nộp vào tay dân phương bắc.
vi.R: Dân Ai Cập sẽ bị sỉ nhục. \q Họ sẽ bị nộp vào tay dân từ phương bắc.

ko.L: 딸 이집트가 수치를 당했다. \q 그가 북쪽 백성의 손에 넘겨졌다.
ko.B: 딸 이집트가 수치를 당하고, \q 북쪽 백성에게 넘겨졌다.
ko.R: 이집트 백성은 수치를 당할 것이다. \q 그들은 북쪽에서 온 백성에게 넘겨질 것이다.

decisions.choice: daughter of Egypt: Egypt pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: As in verses 11 and 19. The poem ends with the proud young woman shamed and handed over.

decisions.choice: the people of the north: Babylon
decisions.reason: From his call Jeremiah spoke of a disaster coming from the north (1:14-15; 6:22). The heading at verse 13 shows that it is Babylon under Nebuchadrezzar; it now falls on Egypt as it fell on Judah.

decisions.choice: will be disgraced ... will be handed over
decisions.reason: Readable puts the past-tense verbs into the future, which is what the prophecy means, and names the people for "daughter".

source.text: אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הִנְנִ֤י פוֹקֵד֙ אֶל־אָמ֣וֹן מִנֹּ֔א וְעַל־פַּרְעֹה֙ וְעַל־מִצְרַ֔יִם וְעַל־אֱלֹהֶ֖יהָ וְעַל־מְלָכֶ֑יהָ וְעַ֨ל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְעַ֥ל הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Behold I [am] punishing Amon of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, and her gods, and her kings, and Pharaoh, and those trusting in him.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel, says: See, I am about to punish Amon of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, and her gods, and her kings, and Pharaoh and those who trust in him.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am about to punish Amon of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt with her gods and her kings, Pharaoh and all who trust in him.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I am going to punish Amon, the god of Thebes. I will punish Pharaoh and Egypt, with her gods and her kings. I will punish Pharaoh and everyone who trusts in him.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice: He aquí, yo castigo a Amón de Tebas, y al faraón, y a Egipto, y a sus dioses, y a sus reyes, y al faraón y a los que confían en él.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice: Voy a castigar a Amón de Tebas, al faraón y a Egipto con sus dioses y sus reyes, al faraón y a todos los que confían en él.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: Voy a castigar a Amón, el dios de Tebas. Castigaré al faraón y a Egipto, con sus dioses y sus reyes. Castigaré al faraón y a todos los que confían en él.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit : Voici, je vais punir Amon de Thèbes, et le pharaon, et l’Égypte, et ses dieux, et ses rois, et le pharaon et ceux qui se confient en lui.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit : Je vais punir Amon de Thèbes, le pharaon, l’Égypte avec ses dieux et ses rois, le pharaon et tous ceux qui se confient en lui.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : Je vais punir Amon, le dieu de Thèbes. Je punirai le pharaon et l’Égypte, avec ses dieux et ses rois. Je punirai le pharaon et tous ceux qui comptent sur lui.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asema: Tazama, nitamwadhibu Amoni wa Thebesi, na Farao, na Misri, na miungu yake, na wafalme wake, naam, Farao na wote wanaomtumaini.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asema: Ninakaribia kumwadhibu Amoni wa Thebesi, na Farao, na Misri pamoja na miungu yake na wafalme wake, Farao na wote wanaomtumaini.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, anasema hivi: Nitamwadhibu Amoni, mungu wa Thebesi. Nitamwadhibu Farao na Misri, pamoja na miungu yake na wafalme wake. Nitamwadhibu Farao na kila mtu anayemtumaini.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phạt A-môn của Thê-bê, Pha-ra-ôn, Ai Cập, các thần và các vua của nó, tức Pha-ra-ôn và những kẻ tin cậy nơi hắn.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sắp trừng phạt A-môn của Thê-bê, Pha-ra-ôn, và Ai Cập cùng các thần và các vua của nó, Pha-ra-ôn và mọi kẻ tin cậy nơi hắn.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán như vầy: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trừng phạt A-môn, thần của thành Thê-bê. Ta sẽ trừng phạt Pha-ra-ôn và Ai Cập, cùng các thần và các vua của nó. Ta sẽ trừng phạt Pha-ra-ôn và mọi kẻ tin cậy nơi hắn.

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님께서 말씀하신다. 보라, 내가 테베의 아몬과 바로와 이집트와 그의 신들과 그의 왕들과, 바로와 그를 의지하는 자들을 벌하겠다.
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님께서 말씀하신다. 내가 테베의 아몬과 바로와 이집트를 그 신들과 왕들과 함께 벌하겠다. 바로와 그를 의지하는 모든 자를 벌하겠다.
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님께서 말씀하신다. 나는 테베의 신 아몬을 벌하겠다. 나는 바로와 이집트를 그 신들과 왕들과 함께 벌하겠다. 나는 바로와 그를 의지하는 모든 사람을 벌하겠다.

decisions.choice: Amon of No: Amon, the god of Thebes
decisions.reason: No is the Hebrew name of Thebes, the great city of Upper Egypt (Ezekiel 30:14-16; Nahum 3:8, "No-amon"). Amon was its chief god, worshiped as king of the gods. The judgment begins with the god on whom Egypt relied.

decisions.choice: punishing her gods: the LORD judges the gods of Egypt
decisions.reason: As at the exodus (Exodus 12:12; Numbers 33:4) and in Jeremiah's sign at Tahpanhes (43:12-13), the LORD's judgment falls on Egypt's gods as well as on its people. The verb is "visit", used of calling to account (verse 21).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh named twice: the stress falls on those who trust in him
decisions.reason: Pharaoh is named in the list and again at the end with "those who trust in him". These include Judeans who looked to Egypt for safety instead of to the LORD (2:36-37; 37:7; 42:13-17; Isaiah 30:1-3; 31:1).

decisions.choice: Thebes
decisions.reason: All levels give No its familiar name Thebes, as Memphis is given for Noph (verse 14). A footnote can give the Hebrew name.

decisions.choice: See, I am about to punish
decisions.reason: The Hebrew opens God's words with a call to attention and a participle of what is about to happen; the wording follows 20:4. Readable repeats "I will punish" to keep the long list clear.

decisions.choice: Tebas
decisions.reason: The Hebrew *No* is the city of Thebes in Upper Egypt, whose god was Amon; every level uses the known name, as the English.

decisions.choice: "Thebesi" for *No* at every level
decisions.reason: As the English: the city is named by its familiar name, Thebes, the city of the god Amon.

decisions.choice: "Thèbes" for *No* at every level
decisions.reason: As the English: the city is given the name readers know.

decisions.choice: A-môn của Thê-bê
decisions.reason: "No" is given as Thebes at every level, as the English does; the god Amon is written A-môn, as the king's name in 2 Kings 21.

decisions.choice: "테베의 아몬"
decisions.reason: As the English, which names Thebes at every level for *No*.

source.text: וּנְתַתִּ֗ים בְּיַד֙ מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשָׁ֔ם וּבְיַ֛ד נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וּבְיַד־עֲבָדָ֑יו וְאַחֲרֵי־כֵ֛ן תִּשְׁכֹּ֥ן כִּֽימֵי־קֶ֖דֶם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will give them into [the] hand of [those] seeking their life, and into [the] hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into [the] hand of his servants; and after this she will dwell as [in the] days of old, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And I will give them into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants. But afterward she will be inhabited as in the days of old, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will hand them over to those who want to kill them, to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and his officials. But afterward Egypt will be lived in again as in former days, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will hand them over to the people who want to kill them. I will hand them over to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and his officials. But later, people will live in Egypt again as they did long ago, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y los entregaré en mano de los que buscan su vida, y en mano de Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y en mano de sus siervos. Pero después será habitada como en los días antiguos, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Los entregaré a los que quieren matarlos, a Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y a sus funcionarios. Pero después Egipto volverá a ser habitado como en tiempos pasados, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Los entregaré a la gente que quiere matarlos. Los entregaré a Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y a sus funcionarios. Pero más tarde la gente volverá a vivir en Egipto como vivía hace mucho tiempo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et je les livrerai dans la main de ceux qui cherchent leur vie, et dans la main de Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, et dans la main de ses serviteurs. Mais après cela, elle sera habitée comme aux jours d’autrefois, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Je les livrerai à ceux qui veulent leur mort, à Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, et à ses officiers. Mais ensuite l’Égypte sera de nouveau habitée comme autrefois, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Je les livrerai aux gens qui veulent les tuer. Je les livrerai à Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, et à ses officiers. Mais plus tard, des gens habiteront de nouveau en Égypte, comme il y a très longtemps, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nami nitawatia mkononi mwa wale wanaoitafuta nafsi yao, na mkononi mwa Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli, na mkononi mwa watumishi wake. Lakini baadaye itakaliwa na watu kama siku za kale, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Nitawakabidhi kwa wale wanaotaka kuwaua, kwa Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli na maafisa wake. Lakini baadaye Misri itakaliwa tena kama siku za zamani, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Nitawakabidhi kwa watu wanaotaka kuwaua. Nitawakabidhi kwa Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli na maafisa wake. Lakini baadaye watu wataishi tena Misri kama walivyoishi zamani, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ta sẽ phó chúng vào tay những kẻ tìm hại mạng sống chúng, vào tay Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn và vào tay các đầy tớ nó. Nhưng về sau, Ai Cập sẽ có người ở như thời xưa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Ta sẽ phó chúng cho những kẻ muốn giết chúng, cho Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn và các quan chức của nó. Nhưng về sau, Ai Cập sẽ lại có người ở như thời xưa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Ta sẽ phó chúng cho những kẻ muốn giết chúng. Ta sẽ phó chúng cho Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn và các quan chức của nó. Nhưng về sau, người ta sẽ lại sống tại Ai Cập như thời xưa, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 그들을 그들의 목숨을 노리는 자들의 손과 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살의 손과 그의 신하들의 손에 넘겨주겠다. 그러나 그 뒤에 그곳은 옛날처럼 사람이 살게 될 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 내가 그들을 그들의 목숨을 노리는 자들, 곧 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살과 그의 신하들에게 넘겨주겠다. 그러나 그 뒤에 이집트에는 옛날처럼 다시 사람이 살 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 나는 그들을 죽이려는 사람들에게 넘겨주겠다. 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살과 그의 신하들에게 넘겨주겠다. 그러나 나중에 이집트에는 오래전처럼 다시 사람들이 살게 될 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: those who seek their life: those who want to kill them
decisions.reason: "Seek someone's life" means to try to kill (4:30; 11:21; 19:7).

decisions.choice: afterward she will be inhabited as in the days of old: Egypt will recover
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine, so its subject is Egypt pictured as a woman. After the judgment the land will be lived in again. Jeremiah gives similar promises for Moab, Ammon and Elam (48:47; 49:6, 39); compare Isaiah 19:22-25 and Ezekiel 29:13-14.

decisions.choice: verse 26 kept, as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: omit the verse with the Greek
decisions.reason: The Greek translation of Jeremiah does not have this verse. The Hebrew text, which this translation follows, has it. This is written from general knowledge (see 1:1).

decisions.choice: his officials
decisions.reason: "Servants" of a king are his court officials, so Balanced and Readable say "officials", as Isaiah does. The name keeps the form Nebuchadrezzar, as in verses 2 and 13.

decisions.choice: Egypt will be lived in again (Balanced); people will live in Egypt again (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Egypt as the subject (m2) and say plainly that "dwell" here means being inhabited.

source.text: וְ֠אַתָּה אַל־תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ וְאַל־תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲק֛וֹב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you, do not fear, my servant Jacob, and do not be dismayed, Israel; for look, I [am] saving you from afar, and your offspring from [the] land of their captivity; and Jacob will return and be quiet and be at ease, and there [will be] none making [him] afraid.

en.L: And you, do not fear, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, and do not be dismayed, Israel, \q for look, I am saving you from far away, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. \q And Jacob will return and be quiet and at ease, and there will be no one to make [him] afraid.
en.B: But you, Jacob {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, do not be afraid; do not be dismayed, Israel. \q For I will save you from a far country, and your descendants from the land where they are captives. \q Jacob will come home and have quiet and rest, and no one will make him afraid.
en.R: But do not be afraid, Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. Israel, do not be frightened. \q I will save you from a land far away. I will save your children from the land where they are prisoners. \q The people of Jacob will come home. They will live in peace and safety, and no one will frighten them.

es.L: Pero tú, no temas, siervo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} Jacob, ni te espantes, Israel, \q porque he aquí, yo te salvo de lejos, y a tu descendencia de la tierra de su cautiverio. \q Y Jacob volverá, y estará tranquilo y seguro, y no habrá quien [lo] atemorice.
es.B: Pero tú, Jacob, siervo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, no tengas miedo; no te espantes, Israel. \q Porque yo te salvaré de un país lejano, y a tus descendientes de la tierra donde están cautivos. \q Jacob volverá a casa y tendrá tranquilidad y reposo, y nadie lo atemorizará.
es.R: Pero no tengas miedo, Jacob, siervo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}. Israel, no te asustes. \q Yo te salvaré de una tierra lejana. Salvaré a tus hijos de la tierra donde están prisioneros. \q El pueblo de Jacob volverá a casa. Vivirá en paz y seguridad, y nadie lo asustará.

fr.L: Et toi, ne crains pas, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Jacob, et ne t’effraie pas, Israël, \q car voici, je te sauve du lointain, et ta descendance du pays de sa captivité. \q Et Jacob reviendra, il sera tranquille et en paix, et personne ne [l’]effraiera.
fr.B: Mais toi, Jacob {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur, n’aie pas peur ; ne t’effraie pas, Israël. \q Car je te sauverai d’un pays lointain, et tes descendants du pays où ils sont captifs. \q Jacob reviendra et vivra dans le calme et le repos, et personne ne lui fera peur.
fr.R: Mais n’aie pas peur, Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur. Israël, ne sois pas effrayé. \q Je te sauverai d’un pays lointain. Je sauverai tes enfants du pays où ils sont prisonniers. \q Le peuple de Jacob reviendra chez lui. Il vivra en paix et en sécurité, et personne ne lui fera peur.

sw.L: Nawe, usiogope, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Yakobo, wala usifadhaike, Israeli, \q kwa maana tazama, ninakuokoa kutoka mbali, na uzao wako kutoka nchi ya utumwa wao. \q Naye Yakobo atarudi na kutulia na kustarehe, wala hakuna atakayemtia hofu.
sw.B: Basi wewe, Yakobo mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, usiogope; usifadhaike, Israeli. \q Kwa maana nitakuokoa kutoka nchi ya mbali, na wazao wako kutoka nchi wanamoshikiliwa mateka. \q Yakobo atarudi nyumbani na kupata utulivu na raha, wala hakuna atakayemtia hofu.
sw.R: Basi usiogope, Yakobo, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Israeli, usitishike. \q Nitakuokoa kutoka nchi ya mbali. Nitawaokoa watoto wako kutoka nchi wanamoshikiliwa kama wafungwa. \q Watu wa Yakobo watarudi nyumbani. Wataishi kwa amani na usalama, wala hakuna atakayewatisha.

vi.L: Còn ngươi, hỡi Gia-cốp đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đừng sợ; hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đừng kinh hãi, \q vì kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cứu ngươi từ phương xa, và dòng dõi ngươi khỏi xứ chúng bị lưu đày. \q Gia-cốp sẽ trở về, được yên tĩnh và an ổn, chẳng còn ai làm [nó] sợ hãi.
vi.B: Vậy, hỡi Gia-cốp đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, con đừng sợ; hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đừng kinh hãi. \q Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cứu con từ một xứ xa xôi, và cứu dòng dõi con khỏi xứ chúng đang bị lưu đày. \q Gia-cốp sẽ trở về, được yên tĩnh và nghỉ ngơi, chẳng còn ai làm nó sợ hãi.
vi.R: Vậy hỡi Gia-cốp đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, con đừng sợ. Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đừng hoảng sợ. \q Ta sẽ cứu con từ một xứ xa xôi. Ta sẽ cứu con cháu con khỏi xứ chúng đang bị giam cầm. \q Dân Gia-cốp sẽ trở về quê hương. Họ sẽ sống bình an và yên ổn, chẳng còn ai làm họ sợ hãi.

ko.L: 그러나 너, 내 종 야곱아, 두려워하지 마라. 이스라엘아, 놀라지 마라. \q 보아라, 내가 너를 먼 곳에서 구원하고, 네 자손을 포로로 잡혀 있는 땅에서 구원하겠다. \q 야곱이 돌아와서 평온하고 안락하게 살 것이며, 아무도 [그를] 두렵게 하지 못할 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 내 종 야곱아, 두려워하지 마라. 이스라엘아, 놀라지 마라. \q 내가 너를 먼 나라에서 구원하고, 네 자손을 포로로 잡혀 있는 땅에서 구원하겠다. \q 야곱이 돌아와서 평온하고 편안하게 살 것이며, 아무도 그를 두렵게 하지 못할 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 내 종 야곱아, 두려워하지 마라. 이스라엘아, 겁내지 마라. \q 내가 먼 나라에서 너를 구원하겠다. 포로로 잡혀 있는 땅에서 네 자손을 구원하겠다. \q 야곱의 자손이 집으로 돌아올 것이다. 그들은 평안하고 안전하게 살 것이며, 아무도 그들을 겁주지 못할 것이다.

decisions.choice: do not fear, my servant Jacob: the words of 30:10, repeated here
decisions.reason: Verses 27-28 repeat 30:10-11 almost word for word, and the wording here follows those verses. Verse 27 differs in one point: 30:10 has "declares the LORD" after "my servant Jacob", and here it is missing (it comes in verse 28). After the oracle against Egypt, the promise turns to Israel: the nation it trusted will fall, but God's people will come home.

decisions.choice: my servant: Israel as the people the LORD has chosen and keeps
decisions.reason: As in 30:10. It is a title of honor, not of bondage (Isaiah 41:8-9; 44:1-2).

decisions.choice: I am saving you from far away: a sure promise, spoken as if already under way
decisions.reason: As in 30:10.

decisions.choice: the wording of 30:10
decisions.reason: The levels keep the wording of 30:10 so that a reader hears the same promise in both places, leaving out only "declares the LORD" (m1). Balanced and Readable begin "But" rather than the "So" of 30:10, because here the promise is set against Egypt's fate.

decisions.choice: The people of Jacob ... They ... them
decisions.reason: As in 30:10.

decisions.choice: the wording of 30:10
decisions.reason: Verses 27-28 repeat 30:10-11, and the Spanish of that passage is reused at each level. Here the Hebrew has no "declares the LORD" in the first line, and verse 28 differs as noted there.

decisions.choice: the Swahili wording of 30:10-11 at each level, reused for 46:27-28
decisions.reason: The promise to Jacob repeats 30:10-11; the same Swahili lets a reader see it, and only what the Hebrew changes is changed: no "declares the LORD" in 46:27, and 46:28 opens with "do not fear" and says "where I have driven you" ("nilikokufukuzia") for "scattered".

decisions.choice: "Jacob reviendra" (L, B), "reviendra chez lui" (R)
decisions.reason: *Shuv* is "revenir" at every level in French Jeremiah, for repentance and return from exile alike. Verses 27-28 repeat 30:10-11: the French keeps the wording of 30:10-11 at each level and changes only what the Hebrew changes (no "declares the LORD" in verse 27; "do not fear, my servant Jacob" and "driven" in verse 28).

decisions.choice: ngươi (L); con (B, R), to Jacob; đầy tớ Ta
decisions.reason: Israel addressed as one person is "ngươi" at Literal and "con" at Balanced and Readable, as the terms note sets; "my servant Jacob" is "Gia-cốp đầy tớ Ta". Verses 27-28 repeat 30:10-11 word for word at each level and change only where the Hebrew changes: "CHÚA phán vậy" is missing in verse 27 and comes in verse 28, verse 28 says "đã đuổi" (driven) for 30:11's "đã làm cho ... tan lạc" (scattered), and it has no "để cứu ngươi".

decisions.choice: Verses 27-28 reuse the Korean draft of 30:10-11 at each level, changing only what the Hebrew changes (no "declares the LORD" in verse 27; "for I am with you" and "driven" in verse 28)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: the words of 30:10-11 repeated here.

source.text: אַ֠תָּה אַל־תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אִתְּךָ֖ אָ֑נִי כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֣ם׀אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִדַּחְתִּ֣יךָ שָׁ֗מָּה וְאֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹא־אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: You, do not fear, my servant Jacob, declares Yahweh, for with you I [am]; for I will make [a] full end of all the nations where I have driven you there, but you I will not make [a] full end [of]; and I will discipline you in justice, and leaving unpunished I will not leave you unpunished.

en.L: You, do not fear, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Jacob, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for I [am] with you. \q For I will make a full end of all the nations where I have driven you, but of you I will not make a full end. \q I will discipline you in just measure, \q and I will by no means leave you unpunished.
en.B: You, Jacob {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, do not be afraid, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because I am with you. \q I will bring to an end all the nations among whom I drove you, but you I will not bring to an end. \q I will discipline you, but justly, \q and I will not let you go unpunished.
en.R: Do not be afraid, Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I am with you. \q I will completely destroy all the nations where I drove you. But I will not completely destroy you. \q I will correct you, but I will be fair, \q and I will not let you escape all punishment.

es.L: Tú, no temas, siervo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}} Jacob, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, porque yo [estoy] contigo. \q Porque acabaré del todo con todas las naciones adonde te he arrojado, pero contigo no acabaré del todo. \q Te corregiré con justa medida, \q y de ninguna manera te dejaré sin castigo.
es.B: Tú, Jacob, siervo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, no tengas miedo, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, porque yo estoy contigo. \q Acabaré con todas las naciones adonde te arrojé, pero contigo no acabaré. \q Te corregiré, pero con justicia, \q y no te dejaré sin castigo.
es.R: No tengas miedo, Jacob, siervo {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Yo estoy contigo. \q Destruiré por completo a todas las naciones adonde te arrojé. Pero a ti no te destruiré por completo. \q Te corregiré, pero seré justo, \q y no dejaré que te libres de todo castigo.

fr.L: Toi, ne crains pas, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Jacob, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, car je [suis] avec toi. \q Car j’anéantirai toutes les nations parmi lesquelles je t’ai chassé, mais toi, je ne t’anéantirai pas. \q Je te corrigerai avec mesure, \q et je ne te laisserai certainement pas impuni.
fr.B: Toi, Jacob {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur, n’aie pas peur, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, car je suis avec toi. \q J’en finirai avec toutes les nations parmi lesquelles je t’ai chassé, mais avec toi, je n’en finirai pas. \q Je te corrigerai, mais avec justice, \q et je ne te laisserai pas impuni.
fr.R: N’aie pas peur, Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je suis avec toi. \q Je détruirai complètement toutes les nations où je t’ai chassé. Mais toi, je ne te détruirai pas complètement. \q Je te corrigerai, mais je serai juste, \q et je ne te laisserai pas échapper à toute punition.

sw.L: Wewe, usiogope, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Yakobo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] pamoja nawe. \q Kwa maana nitayakomesha kabisa mataifa yote nilikokufukuzia, lakini wewe sitakukomesha kabisa. \q Nitakurudi kwa kipimo cha haki, \q wala sitakuacha kamwe bila adhabu.
sw.B: Wewe, Yakobo mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, usiogope, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niko pamoja nawe. \q Nitayamaliza kabisa mataifa yote ambamo nilikufukuzia, lakini wewe sitakumaliza. \q Nitakuadibisha, lakini kwa haki, \q wala sitakuacha bila adhabu.
sw.R: Usiogope, Yakobo, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mimi niko pamoja nawe. \q Nitayaangamiza kabisa mataifa yote nilikokufukuzia. Lakini wewe sitakuangamiza kabisa. \q Nitakurekebisha, lakini nitakuwa wa haki, \q wala sitakuacha uepuke adhabu yote.

vi.L: Hỡi Gia-cốp đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, ngươi đừng sợ, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở với ngươi. \q Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tận diệt mọi dân tộc mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đuổi ngươi đến, còn ngươi thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không tận diệt. \q Ta sẽ sửa phạt ngươi theo mức công bằng, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chắc chắn không để ngươi khỏi bị phạt.
vi.B: Hỡi Gia-cốp đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, con đừng sợ, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ở với con. \q Ta sẽ tận diệt mọi dân tộc mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đuổi con đến, nhưng con thì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không tận diệt. \q Ta sẽ sửa phạt con, nhưng cách công bằng, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không để con khỏi bị phạt.
vi.R: Hỡi Gia-cốp đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, con đừng sợ, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. Ta ở với con. \q Ta sẽ tiêu diệt hoàn toàn mọi dân tộc nơi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đuổi con đến. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không tiêu diệt con hoàn toàn. \q Ta sẽ sửa dạy con, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ công bằng, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không để con thoát mọi hình phạt.

ko.L: 내 종 야곱아, 너는 두려워하지 마라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 내가 너와 함께 있기 때문이다. \q 내가 너를 쫓아 보낸 모든 민족은 완전히 멸망시키겠지만, 너만은 완전히 멸망시키지 않겠다. \q 내가 너를 법도에 따라 징계하겠고, \q 결코 너를 벌하지 않은 채 두지는 않겠다.
ko.B: 내 종 야곱아, 두려워하지 마라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 너와 함께 있다. \q 내가 너를 쫓아 보낸 모든 민족은 끝장을 내겠지만, 너만은 끝장내지 않겠다. \q 내가 너를 징계하되 공정하게 하겠고, \q 너를 벌하지 않고 그냥 두지는 않겠다.
ko.R: 내 종 야곱아, 두려워하지 마라. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 내가 너와 함께 있다. \q 내가 너를 쫓아 보낸 모든 나라는 완전히 멸망시키겠다. 그러나 너는 완전히 멸망시키지 않겠다. \q 내가 너를 바로잡겠지만 공정하게 하겠다. \q 그러나 너를 아무 벌도 없이 그냥 두지는 않겠다.

decisions.choice: the words of 30:11, with three differences
decisions.reason: The verse follows 30:11 closely. It differs in three places. It opens by repeating "do not fear, my servant Jacob" with "declares the LORD", which here moves from verse 27. It says "for I am with you" without the words "to save you" that follow in 30:11. And it says "where I have driven you" where 30:11 has "where I have scattered you". It also joins "but you I will not make a full end" with a plain "and" where 30:11 has a stronger "only". The promise is the same.

decisions.choice: a full end: complete destruction
decisions.reason: As in 30:11.

decisions.choice: discipline you in justice: correct you in fair measure, not to destroy you
decisions.reason: As in 30:11 (compare 10:24).

decisions.choice: leaving unpunished I will not leave you unpunished: I will certainly not let you go free of punishment
decisions.reason: As in 30:11.

decisions.choice: the wording of 30:11; driven (Literal); drove (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The levels keep the wording of 30:11 wherever the Hebrew is the same, and change only where it differs (m1): the repeated opening, "I am with you" on its own, and "driven" or "drove" for "scattered".

decisions.choice: I will correct you, but I will be fair
decisions.reason: As in 30:11.

decisions.choice: the wording of 30:11
decisions.reason: The Spanish of 30:11 is kept where the Hebrew is the same. Here the verse opens with "do not fear, my servant Jacob" and has no "to save you". It also has "where I have driven you" (arrojado) where 30:11 has "scattered".
